name: sol_integrations_chainlink_ccip_3
description: Chainlink CCIP receiver decodes cross-chain message data with mismatched encoding/type structure
question: The source file in `source` implements a Chainlink CCIP receiver (e.g. `_ccipReceive` or similar handling `any2EvmMessage.data`) that decodes the incoming `data` field using `abi.decode` with a type signature, struct layout, or parameter order that does not match the ABI encoding used when the message was constructed on the source chain, causing corrupted, misinterpreted, or reverted cross-chain data without validating the decoded structure against the expected sender-side encoding, excluding cases where encoding and decoding use identical, explicitly declared types and structure on both chains.
criteria: _ccipReceive decodes any2EvmMessage.data with abi.decode(data, (uint256, address)) while the sender encodes abi.encode(address, uint256, bytes), causing field values to be swapped

Receiver assumes a fixed-size tuple decode of any2EvmMessage.data but the sender conditionally encodes variable-length arrays or structs depending on message type, leading to decode reverts or garbage values
_ccipReceive calls abi.decode(any2EvmMessage.data, (MyStruct)) without checking that the struct definition matches the version used by the sending contract, so upgraded sender payloads are misdecoded

Receiver blindly casts decoded bytes into an address without validating that the encoded value is a proper 20-byte address, allowing malformed cross-chain payloads to be misinterpreted as arbitrary addresses
